=== FILE: 5 ULTIMATE Isometric Exercises for More Core Power and Full Body Stability (Bench, Squat and More!) [ti3po9y8MJ8].en.txt ===

what's up everybody phil bleckman with barban.com and today we're going to talk about some isometric movements that are the best for core strength and full body stability if you want to learn anything about isometric movements in particular just head over to google type in isometric bar bend and all of that information is going to come up there's a lot to cover so let's get into it so let's dive right in with the paused squat whether performing the movement with body weight or with a barbell the squat is a stable movement pattern in nearly every trainee's repertoire the paused squat is more of a modification than a new movement the lifter pauses at the bottom of the lift removing momentum from the bottom so that they have to produce more force in order to stand back up you can pause anywhere during the squat although breaking at the bottom is the most common you'll accumulate more strength and muscle building tension under the load as you're holding it for an extended period of time and pause squats are challenging so you may not need as much weight on the barbell as you would normally use for a squat session moving on we're going to talk about the paused bench press much like the squat the paused bench press takes advantage of removing constant movement throughout the range of motion to focus on control and precision additionally you're going to develop more pressing power as you need to produce more force to get the barbell from a dead stop over your chest when using paused bench press reps the pause bench press forces you to slow the movement down and press with control which means you'll need to dial in the mechanics of your bench press in order to lock it out safely the pause deadlift is a popular deadlift variation among powerlifters and strongmen to develop more strength coming off of the floor typically the lifter pulls the bar off of the ground pauses at the shin and then finishes the pull to the lockout pausing at the shin creates a lot of tension in the hamstrings and lower back and fortifying these areas is a must for effective and efficient deadlifts they are after all critical players in this compound movement benefits of paused deadlifts include learning how to brace better during the deadlift specifically essential for bracing your spine when pulling heavy weight and you'll build stronger hamstrings glutes and quads the front plank may seem like a vanilla movement but it provides some of the best value for no equipment out there planking is likely one of the first exercises to come to mind when considering an isometric exercise and for good reason a well-taught front plank is the cornerstone for conceptualizing and implementing full-body isometric tension across a multitude of exercises from the pause squat to the overhead carry to the deadlift to everything else benefits of the front plank include better developed anti-extension isometric core strength learning the ability to generate full body tension and it can be performed anywhere with or without additional load next up we have the ab wheel rollout the ab wheel is a stable piece of equipment in most commercial and home gyms alike but often gets misused due to a lack of understanding of its proper technique the ab wheel is like a dynamic front plank the front plank is an entirely stationary isometric hold the ab wheel takes the front plank and forces the trainee to resist losing position while the rest of the body moves throughout the range of motion benefits of the ab wheel roll out include integrating front plank technique into a dynamic challenge integrating hip and shoulder mobility into the movement and it requires no additional weight so it can be performed more or less anywhere those are just five isometric exercises you can use to improve your core strength and overall full body mobility if you want to learn any other isometric movements just head over to google type in isometric bar bend and all of that's going to come up we specifically have an article that touches on 11 isometric movements that can benefit your training so next time you head into the gym add some isometric training into your routine to really build out that core strength and full body stability i'm phil blackman for barbadon.com thanks for watching you

exercises like jogging can be a huge asset to strength athletes they can put a lot of strain on the body adding hours on the treadmill to your training might not be the most effective cardio option if your recovery isn't perfectly catered to that plan since your feet remain planted during even the most explosive kettlebell moves you won't be placing the same repetitive strain on your joints and connective tissue as running will many kettlebell exercises are ballistic in nature making them ideal for low impact cardiovascular training benefit number two full body strength part of the magic of strength from working with kettlebells with a particular emphasis on the core benefit number three coordination and mobility to train effectively with kettlebells you've got to be both coordinated and mobile you can't perform a proper kettlebell snatch without sufficient full-body coordination there's no way you'll be able to nail such a complex move if you don't have enough kinesthetic awareness to slip your hand into the right position above your head without slapping the bell on your forearm you also need sufficient shoulder mobility and overhead stability to settle the weight in the top position the good news is that you don't have to start kettlebell training with good coordination or mobility you can start small you can build overhead mobility coordination and stability with moves like turkish getups and kettlebell windmills you'll develop better hip mobility and coordination through training deep kettlebell goblet squats and proper kettlebell deadlifts and swings by the time four in the morning to get a good workout the versatility offered by kettlebell training is a key benefit of these implements you can literally work out anywhere with kettlebells all within the space taken up by a yoga mat there's more to it than just train anywhere advantages to kettlebells the versatility offered by kettlebells means that you can train with completely different movement patterns that you might be used to kettlebells help you add challenges that are substantial even at sub-maximal loads this means less stress to your body overall while stimulating growth in new areas of your strength and athleticism benefit number five fight imbalances with asymmetries some kettlebell moves like swings and dead bug pullovers require both hands on the bell but most kettlebell exercises are unilateral in nature this means that you either perform reps with one side at a time or have one bell in each hand so your arms work independently this means that strength and muscle asymmetries don't stand much of a chance in the face of kettlebell training plus if aesthetics are your goal balancing your strength can help you equally stimulate each side of your body benefit number six power development grinding out a difficult lift takes a tremendous amount of mental discipline but moving weights quickly takes a different kind of skill and mental toughness kettlebells can help you become a more powerful lifter from swings and cleans to snatches and high pulls many staple kettlebell lifts require you to move the heavy weight quickly you'll find that the more you practice with more adept at your barbell sport and finally benefit number seven grip strength of course well your whole body will get stronger while working with kettlebells your grip strength is worth mentioning in particular kettlebell training often involves timed circuits or flows during which you don't drop the bell for minutes at a time a huge contrast to the bursts of barbell work kettlebells are also
